gate_text: Per-round BSS breakdown (R64 -> NCG). Does the ceiling hold uniformly or break in E8/F4?
verdict: Seed dominance weakens in later rounds (E8 42.6% upset rate vs R64 24.6%) but seed-independent signals still do not add value in any round (BSS ~0 everywhere except n=17 NCG outlier). Ceiling is NOT uniform; but the non-uniformity does not open an exploitable gap for prediction-accuracy improvement.

headline_findings.ceiling_is_non_uniform: YES: E8 upset rate 42.6% vs R64 24.6%; +18.0pp gap. Seed dominance weakens.
headline_findings.but_si_still_does_not_help: YES across every round: max |BSS| = 0.033 at NCG (n=17), otherwise |BSS| <= 0.018. No round shows a practically meaningful positive BSS with statistical power.

effect_on_pivot: CONSISTENT with 2026-04-02 pivot (row 7). The round-specific view reinforces rather than challenges the BSS=0 claim: even in the highest-upset round (E8, 42.6% rate), seed-independent signals show BSS=-1.0% (slightly worse than seed). If there were a round where ML helps, this is where it would show up. It does not.
